newsitem.title: UK: Buba's Jochimsen says budget fudging order of day.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Jochimsen says budget fudging order of day.

text.p: Budgetary fudging has become the order of the day in the drive towards European economic and monetary union, Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said.
In an article for the European newspaper, he criticised what he called attempts to create "problem-solving councils and pacts" which contravened the Maastricht Treaty.

"The same lack of trust is generated by the ease with which budgetary fudging has become the order of the day to fulfil formally the criteria of the Maastricht Treaty," Jochimsen wrote in an article to be published on Thursday.
Jochimsen said that at the EU summit in Dublin in December, there had been a growing understanding that a stable euro needed solid, sustainable public finances in all member states.
"But that's too good to be true, because upon closer scrutiny the stability pact still lacks substance," he said.
The pact did not contain proposed sanctions against countries running deficits or any rule that required such countries to prove why they should be exempt from fines, Jochimsen said.
An ineffective stability pact meant the Maastricht Treaty's conditions for EMU entry risked losing their effect.
"Already there is talk of determining violations of the stability agreement 'on a case-by-case basis'," he said.
Anybody seeking this solution might swiftly have to deal with a "coalition of sinners" which might lead to a weak and unstable euro and, in effect, a strong dollar.
"The final act -- the abolition of Europe's anchor currency, the deutschemark, in exchange for a weak common one -- could turn out to be a dubious contribution to EU integration," he wrote.
"There is not yet enough trust and confidence to make the new euro a stable and strong currency as intended by the treaty."
